subject: Can runMI use datasets multiply imputed by SPSS?

messages.author: f6258e8f3a96b714
messages.subject: Can runMI use datasets multiply imputed by SPSS?
parts:
Hi 
I have datasets that were multiply imputed within SPSS.
I imported them into R, checked they were stored as dataframes.
I made a list of the dataframes and confirmed they were type list.

When I ran runMI, I received:
Error in (function (model = NULL, dataList = NULL, dataFunction = NULL, : lavaan ERROR: (generated) data is not a data.frame (or a matrix)

Is there any additional information generated by the R MI procedures that would be needed for runMI to use these datasets?

Thanks
Dr Matthew Smout

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Can runMI use datasets multiply imputed by SPSS?
parts: You have only provided an error message.  If you can provide a minimal syntax example that leads to this error (show us how you do the things you describe), there might be some clues.  If not, some accompanying data would make it a full reprex.

messages.subject: Re: Can runMI use datasets multiply imputed by SPSS?
parts:
Background: I have tested a path model (Path.mod) which runs nicely on the set with complete responses. 

RawResult.fit <-sem(Path.mod, Study1_OR)

I wanted to run the same model on a set of 5 imputed sets from SPSS. These were imported into dataframes via RStudio import dialogue.

 

Problem:

I tried two methods of creating a list of dataframes for use with RunMI.

(1)

MIMPS <- list(Study1_OR, Study1_IMP1, Study1_IMP2, Study1_IMP3, Study1_IMP4, Study1_IMP5) 

verified:

> is.data.frame(Study1_IMP1) [1] TRUE

(repeated for each df)

> is.list(MIMPS) [1] TRUE

 

Trying to use runMI by:

Result.fit <- runMI(Path.mod, datalist=MIMPS, fun = "sem")

 

gave following error:

> Result.fit <- runMI(Path.mod, datalist=MIMPS, fun = "sem") Error in (function (model = NULL, dataList = NULL, dataFunction = NULL, : lavaan ERROR: (generated) data is not a data.frame (or a matrix)

 

 

(2)

Study1_IMP1$.imp <- 1
Study1_IMP2$.imp <- 2
Study1_IMP3$.imp <- 3
Study1_IMP4$.imp <- 4
Study1_IMP5$.imp <- 5
Study1_OR$.imp <-0
Imp_Long <-rbind(Study1_OR, Study1_IMP1, Study1_IMP2, Study1_IMP3, Study1_IMP4, Study1_IMP5)

 

Running this 

Result.fit <- runMI(Path.mod, Imp_Long, m=5, fun = "sem")

gave a different error:

 

> Result.fit <- runMI(Path.mod, Imp_Long, m=5, fun = "sem") The resulting variance matrix was not invertible. Please check your data for highly collinear variables. The resulting variance matrix was not invertible. Please check your data for highly collinear variables. The resulting variance matrix was not invertible. Please check your data for highly collinear variables. The resulting variance matrix was not invertible. Please check your data for highly collinear variables. Bivariate correlations suggest the strongest Pearson correlation is .83, there are 4 others over .7.  I guess these may be near the cusp of multicollinearity but the error message lists a greater number of variables that are perfectly collinear than would be between .7 & .85.

Kind regards
Matthew
